registrar_rulings.reason: The existing weekly id `tortillas` IS the flour-tortilla commodity - its commodities.json label is literally 'Tortillas (flour)' (line 9898), it is live-priced at $0.106/each across 7 stores (Walmart cheapest), and the estate already splits the other forms out under their own ids (corn-tortillas at $0.0561/each, high-fiber-tortillas excluded by pattern). 'Large' is not a variant here: the row's large/burrito/XL excludes fire only in combination with carb-balance/high-fiber terms, so plain large flour tortillas are in scope. Same food, same form, already priced - minting flour-tortillas would be exactly the bread-crumbs/breadcrumbs defect. Follow-up: add `flour-tortillas -> tortillas` to recipe-floor-id-map.json (units match: each). Separately, if the vocabulary needs a Flour Tortillas name row, that is a name ruling, not an id - fdc:175037 is the plausible macros row but transcribe a label before trusting it.

The mapper was right to refuse the cheddar-cheese-shredded bridge (a cheddar/jack blend is not a bag of shredded cheddar), but the estate's pricing id for this purchase class is the GENERIC `shredded-cheese` ('Shredded / Block Cheese', $0.1521/oz at Sam's Club, 7 stores): its include net already captures blend bags via 'shredded\s+\w+(?:\s+\w+)?\s+cheese' and '(cheddar|mozzarella|colby|monterey|jack)\s+cheese' - a 'Shredded Mexican Blend Cheese' label matches today and would be claimed by this row, so a new id would price the SAME shelf products twice. The declared-same-thing layer already collapses cheddar-cheese-shredded AND mozzarella-cheese into shredded-cheese (both alias_of in the live feed at the identical crown), which is the human-ratified convention that shredded-bag varieties share one price id. Follow-up: add `mexican-blend-cheese -> shredded-cheese` to recipe-floor-id-map.json (units match: oz, 8 oz bag). The vocabulary/macros question is separate: fdc:171288 'Cheese, Mexican blend' is a credible macros row for the NAME, but that mints no id.

macro_cross_check: Computed over all 10 lines at source scale (8 servings): 3545 cal / 200.1 g protein / 314 g carbs = 443 cal, 25.0 g protein, 39.3 g carbs per serving. Source published 624 / 44 / 44. PROTEIN GAP -43%, far outside the 15% bar, so I re-examined the portions as rule 6 requires - and the gap is NOT ours. No each-weight assumption is in play: the main protein is written out as '1 pound lean ground beef' for 8 servings, which is 57 g raw per serving, and the instructions confirm 1 tortilla and 2 cups of cheese total per 8 enchiladas. 57 g of raw 93/7 beef (12.2 P) plus 28 g of cheese (6.6 P) plus one tortilla (5.7 P) is 24.5 g of protein, and there is no fourth protein on the page. The published 44 g cannot be reached from this ingredient list at any serving count (at 4 servings it would be 50 P but also 886 cal). I believe the SOURCE'S published block is wrong, not our grams, and I am flagging it rather than inflating a portion to chase it.
